prediction.likelyOutcome: Aklilu is a reasonably strong favorite to recover the undisputed fixtures/equipment value (~$171,510) but faces a genuine, legally-grounded risk that his $238,716 cost-to-create goodwill figure will be discounted or rejected because that methodology sits uneasily with the earnings-based definition of compensable goodwill under CCP 1263.510 that Mamaux's testimony tracks more closely; a split verdict crediting a reduced goodwill award is the most probable trial outcome, with total recovery well above the Agency's $35,000 offer but below Aklilu's $355,668 demand.

figures.label: Pedersen cost-to-create goodwill valuation
figures.quote: concluded Auto Inn had adjusted annual losses of $35,000, $37,000, $49,000, $53,000, $52,000 and $12,000 in the years 1998 through 2003, for a total loss of $238,716

figures.label: Fixtures and equipment (Pedersen appraisal)
figures.quote: the value of the fixtures and equipment ($171,510)

outcome.description: The jury found Aklilu suffered lost goodwill of $200,000 (his expert said $238,716; the Agency's said none). In a separate proceeding the court apportioned $4,265 of the $34,525 paid for fixtures and equipment to Aklilu (not included here), denied his motion for litigation expenses, and gave the Agency a setoff against interest for post-possession rent. The Second District affirmed on July 30, 2007 (rehearing denied and opinion modified August 20, 2007), approving the 'cost to create' goodwill valuation.
